Peak and late sampling windows were deliberately chosen to contrast scarce versus high pollinator activity. Legitimate oil-bee visit marks occurred on 7.5% of peak flowers (134) versus 93.6% of late flowers (140). The binomial seed-set model reports flowering-time estimate +1.55 (SE 0.25), treatment +1.41 (SE 0.24), and interaction -1.26 (SE 0.31); together with the reported group pattern these signs identify +1.55 as the late-versus-peak natural-pollination log-odds contrast. Variance=0.25^2. Model n=173 plants across flowering-time × pollination-treatment groups. Dataset is available upon request.

Timing-extreme contrast fixed from partner activity before using fitness values: predator moths concentrate oviposition in mid- to late July; HA flowers in mid-July (high overlap) and HD in early to late August (low overlap). Table 1 final fruit-set rate (intact fruits/perfect flowers): HA mean=0.13 SD=0.19 n=177; HD mean=0.40 SD=0.29 n=127. Native effect is Hedges g for high-overlap HA minus low-overlap HD, reconstructed with pooled SD and small-sample J correction; g=-1.1368391965, variance=0.0155963310. This is observational across permanent plots and retains programme-level dependence.

Early experiment is the measured Hadena-dominant/high-overlap window; late experiment is the co-pollinator-dominant/low-Hadena-overlap window. Successful fruits are initiated fruits free from H. ectypa predation and are the paper's female reproductive-success measure. Table 1 reports early mean=2.66 SE=2.95 n=59 and late mean=3.91 SE=4.13 n=58. Source-labeled SEs are converted to SD via SE*sqrt(n), then Hedges g is reconstructed for high-overlap early minus low-overlap late: g=-0.0453662495, variance=0.0337540056.

Strict contrast restricted to 2007 because bumble-bee activity was measured contemporaneously only that year. Early/mid-July had very low visits by queens; worker bees appeared in late July and visit frequency increased abruptly and stayed high through August. Table 4 intact natural seed set: HIS M high-overlap mean=0.77 SE=0.03 n=24 versus E low-overlap mean=0.62 SE=0.04 n=24. Source values are mean±SE; SD=SE*sqrt(n), then Hedges g for M minus E gives g=0.8518282660, variance=0.0885105687.

2015 flowering onset was manipulated into four weekly cohorts (n=10 each). Pollinator visitation was measured contemporaneously and declined >5-fold from week 1 to week 4, fixing week 1 as the higher-availability window before using seed-set values. Dissertation Table 2.2 reports relative observed seed-set means [0.85,1.00,0.91,0.69]; the same four-group outcome has F(3,36)=1.01. For the balanced design, F=MS_between/MS_within deterministically recovers pooled within-group variance on the same relative scale. Hedges g for high-overlap week 1 minus low-overlap week 4 is +0.3732395638, variance=0.1873253239. The common relative scaling cancels in the SMD; no missing variance or slope conversion is used.

Controlled partner-arrival experiment on one synchronously fruiting tree. Receptivity onset defines plant timing and a single pollinator was introduced to randomly chosen syconia at exact ages. Native exposure is partner arrival minus receptivity onset, so day 24 is higher mismatch than day 0. Table 1 mature total seeds: day24 mean=24.15 SD=15.80 n=54; day0 mean=52.85 SD=19.99 n=33. Hedges g for high mismatch minus matching is -1.6258967235, variance=0.0635115103; exposure_direction=mismatch orients this to +1.6258967235 for greater synchrony. Syconia are the source-declared treatment units; all remain one programme dependence cluster. Across all 422 introduced syconia, 33 aborted and abortion frequency did not differ by age; Table 1 seed summaries cover the 389 syconia completing development.
